goals: Mechanistic: characterize the seasonal cycle and magnitude of ET across the Passaic basin and attribute it to land cover and soil controls
Validation: compare simulated ET to local eddy-covariance flux-tower measurements
key_processes: evapotranspiration partitioning (canopy transpiration vs soil evaporation vs canopy interception)
seasonal phenology / leaf-area control on transpiration
soil-moisture limitation of ET in summer

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM directly simulates the full ET partition and its seasonal cycle as a function of land cover and soil, which are the two candidate drivers and both pullable levers. Spatial sampling across the basin's land-cover/soil heterogeneity is the natural mode.

answerable: seasonal ET cycle (amplitude, timing, summer magnitude) at each column
land-cover control on ET partitioning (urban vs forest vs wetland vs agriculture)
soil-texture modulation of summer water-limited ET
spatial variability of ET across the basin from stratified columns

not_answerable.aspect: validation of ET against local eddy-covariance flux towers
not_answerable.why: brief lists EC flux towers under observations_missing — no in-domain EC data exist in the stack, so ET cannot be validated co-located
not_answerable.needs: eddy-covariance (AmeriFlux/FLUXNET) ingest, plus at minimum an analog EC site outside the domain

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 dominant land-cover classes crossed with 3 SSURGO texture classes = 12 cells; implausible combos pruned and replaced with light replication in the two dominant classes (urban, forest). This is the smallest set that spans the ET-controlling heterogeneity of a small, low-relief, urbanized basin.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample wetland/riparian corridors along the mainstem and tributaries where summer ET is water-supply-controlled and groundwater-coupled; place urban and forest columns on their representative soils; avoid stratifying on the weak ~390 m elevation axis since NLDAS at 12 km barely resolves it across this small basin.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light — one extra column each in urban and forest (the areally dominant classes) on a second common soil, to check within-class robustness.

sampling_plan.reason: Impervious-dominant land cover is areally dominant in Passaic; isolates suppressed transpiration and altered partitioning under urban surfaces.
Forest sets the deep-rooted transpiration signal; two soils test soil-texture modulation of summer water-limited ET.
Water-supply-rich riparian zones; isolates the high, less-summer-limited ET end-member and groundwater-coupled evaporation.
Shallow-rooted managed vegetation with distinct phenology; brackets crop/grass ET seasonality against soil texture.

validation_design.comparison: analog — only via an out-of-domain AmeriFlux site with comparable land cover/climate (e.g. a NJ/mid-Atlantic forest or wetland tower), explicitly labelled as analog process validation, NOT co-located; cannot validate the requested Passaic ET directly
validation_design.metric: seasonal-cycle bias and RMSE of monthly ET; correlation of phenological timing
validation_design.n_validation_points: 0 in-domain; 1+ analog sites only if an EC ingest is built

validation_design.comparison: co-located at wells near riparian columns — weak indirect check on the water-supply state driving riparian ET; requires spin-up / WTD warm start and lacks lateral flow, so interpret as consistency check only
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on well density near sampled columns

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing (nearest 12 km cell), native SSURGO soil, land-cover-appropriate PFT; WTD-informed warm start for riparian columns

requires_capabilities.why: the user's explicit validation target is EC-tower ET, which is not in the data stack
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire ET validation goal (co-located); even analog validation needs this ingest

requires_capabilities.capability: out-of-domain analog site selection for EC
requires_capabilities.why: no in-domain towers exist, so any ET validation must borrow a comparable AmeriFlux site
requires_capabilities.blocks: labelled analog ET validation as a fallback

requires_capabilities.why: riparian ET is groundwater-coupled and any well-based WTD check needs realistic initial water table
requires_capabilities.blocks: meaningful riparian ET and the secondary WTD consistency check

requires_capabilities.why: to use the available well observations as an indirect state check

assumptions: Passaic land cover is dominated by urban/developed with substantial forest, wetland/riparian, and some agriculture — used to set the four land-cover strata (needs confirmation from a land-cover data source).
SSURGO texture classes (sandy/loam/clay) are the relevant soil strata; actual dominant textures to be resolved from gridded soil.
The ~390 m relief over this small basin is too weak, at 12 km NLDAS resolution, to warrant an elevation stratification axis.
open_questions: Is any eddy-covariance site (in- or near-domain) acceptable as an analog, or must validation be dropped and reframed as unvalidated characterization?
Should we attempt a streamflow-based water-balance sanity check using the USGS gauges, which would require a runoff aggregation/routing capability the single-column stack lacks?
Which specific years (1980-2018) best represent 'normal' seasonal ET, or is a multi-year climatology desired?
